snippets.body: The National Women's Hall of Fame is the nation's first and oldest nonprofit organization and museum dedicated to honoring and celebrating the achievements of distinguished American women.
snippets.attribution: National Women's Hall of Fame · Our History — https://www.womenofthehall.org/about/our-history/

snippets.body: Since 1973, the National Women's Hall of Fame has honored distinguished American women whose achievements have shaped our world.
snippets.attribution: National Women's Hall of Fame · Induction 2026 — https://www.womenofthehall.org/induction-2026/

snippets.body: Despite making up over half the population, women and girls receive less than 2% of philanthropic giving in the U.S.
snippets.attribution: National Women's Hall of Fame · Ways to Give — https://www.womenofthehall.org/ways-to-give/

snippets.body: Shirley Hartley envisioned a (National) Women's Hall of Fame in Seneca Falls, the birthplace of the Women's Rights Movement.
snippets.attribution: National Women's Hall of Fame · Our History — https://www.womenofthehall.org/about/our-history/

snippets.body: Dr. Kristen Oehlrich is the CEO and Executive Director of the National Women's Hall of Fame, where she leads efforts to expand the Hall's national presence, deepen its educational impact, and celebrate the extraordinary achievements of American women.
snippets.attribution: National Women's Hall of Fame · Our Leadership — https://www.womenofthehall.org/about/our-leadership/

snippets.body: She believed the women's right to vote was a necessary foundation for all other advances.
snippets.attribution: National Women's Hall of Fame · Susan B. Anthony Inductee Profile — https://www.womenofthehall.org/inductee/susan-b-anthony/

snippets.body: For over thirty years, she traveled the country ceaselessly working for women's rights.
snippets.attribution: National Women's Hall of Fame · Susan B. Anthony Inductee Profile — https://www.womenofthehall.org/inductee/susan-b-anthony/

snippets.body: The National Women's Hall of Fame relies on the generosity of individuals, families, foundations, corporations, and granting agencies
snippets.attribution: National Women's Hall of Fame · Our Building — https://www.womenofthehall.org/about/our-building/

snippets.body: The National Women's Hall of Fame project received $1 million in funding from the Downtown Revitalization Initiative
snippets.attribution: NY Governor's Office · Governor Hochul Announces Completion of Improvements to the National Women's Hall of Fame — https://www.governor.ny.gov/news/governor-hochul-announces-completion-improvements-national-womens-hall-fame-part-seneca-falls

snippets.body: In 2007, after nearly a decade of searching for a new building, the National Women's Hall of Fame made a bold decision to purchase the historic Seneca Knitting Mill at 1 Canal Street in Seneca Falls.
snippets.attribution: National Women's Hall of Fame · Our Building — https://www.womenofthehall.org/about/our-building/

snippets.body: Our recent renovations have ensured the Hall is accessible to wheelchair users and other visitors who may need to avoid stairs.
snippets.attribution: National Women's Hall of Fame · Visit Us — https://www.womenofthehall.org/visit/

snippets.body: Nominees are evaluated based on several criteria. These include their impact—whether on a global, national, or field-specific scale—the significance of their accomplishments or work, and the duration over which they have achieved success.
snippets.attribution: National Women's Hall of Fame · Induction 2026 — https://www.womenofthehall.org/induction-2026/

snippets.body: The National Women's Hall of Fame was incorporated as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.
snippets.attribution: National Women's Hall of Fame · Our History — https://www.womenofthehall.org/about/our-history/

snippets.body: Loyalty to the mission of the museum and to the public it serves is the essence of museum work, whether volunteer or paid.
snippets.attribution: American Alliance of Museums · AAM Code of Ethics for Museums — https://www.aam-us.org/programs/ethics-standards-and-professional-practices/code-of-ethics-for-museums/

snippets.body: Museums in the United States are grounded in the tradition of public service. They are organized as public trusts, holding their collections and information as a benefit for those they were established to serve.
snippets.attribution: American Alliance of Museums · AAM Code of Ethics for Museums — https://www.aam-us.org/programs/ethics-standards-and-professional-practices/code-of-ethics-for-museums/

snippets.body: We hold these truths to be self-evident; that all men and women are created equal
snippets.attribution: National Park Service · Declaration of Sentiments (Women's Rights National Historical Park) — https://www.nps.gov/wori/learn/historyculture/declaration-of-sentiments.htm

snippets.body: From 1844 to 1999, the Seneca Knitting Mill produced woolen goods, creating economic opportunities for many generations of residents.
snippets.attribution: National Women's Hall of Fame · Our Building — https://www.womenofthehall.org/about/our-building/
